input.brief: Open-source SEO and AI visibility platform for engineers, founders, and AI coding agents

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Control that reads the page
hero.blueprint: A near-black or deep neutral ground split into two halves by tone alone: the right half is one step lighter than the left, and they meet at a clean vertical edge at 50%. Left half: a small logo mark top-left at a 40px margin, then two-thirds of empty ground, then everything else anchored bottom-left, 40px from the edges: a one-line headline at clamp(26px, 2.1vw, 32px) in medium weight, one supporting sentence at 17px in the softer ink held to 44ch, and the single action as a light rectangular button. Right half: one fragment of the product, centred, about 450px square, built in HTML and working. It is the product's defining control (a loupe, a picker, a dial, a field) and it acts on the page itself: it reads the real background colour, the real headline size or the pointer position and prints that value in its own readout at 13px. Mark its root with data-ui so the product's own radii and borders apply inside it. There is no navigation bar; one text link sits top-right at 15px.
hero.mobile: The halves stack as two tones. The fragment comes first: 78vw square, centred in the lighter block, which is 58svh tall, still live and reading the page under the visitor's finger. The darker block below holds the headline at 6.4vw on up to two lines, the sentence at 16px and the button, left-aligned at 20px. The logo mark sits top-left over the first block.
hero.headline: One plain line at 26–32px naming what the tool is, up to about 32 characters, wrapping to two lines on a phone.

type.note: A light grotesque with open, slightly old-fashioned shapes; large headings look airy and the text weight beneath stays easy to read. Suits AI and research products, fashion houses and calm brand sites.

palette.name: Three stones
palette.note: Three close stone tones share the interface: the lightest for the page, the middle one for panels, the darkest for a single band, all with charcoal type. Saturated colour is left to the photographs and their backdrops; the grey-green fills the button only.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Output index, live sheet
sections.blueprint: For products that make documents: invoices, reports, emails, statements. Columns 1–5 list the names of three to five outputs, one per line, at clamp(36px, 4vw, 64px), leading 1.1, each a `<button>`; the selected name is in full ink, the rest in the soft ink. There is no other heading. Columns 7–12 are a stage in a flat tone one step from the ground, 88svh tall, and on it lies the selected output as an object: a paper-white sheet 560px wide, built in HTML at true size, root marked data-ui, with a real sender, real line items, sums that add up and a date. The sheet starts 72px below the stage's top and runs past its bottom edge, which crops it. Selecting a name swaps the sheet with a 200ms crossfade; an email is narrower (440px), a receipt narrower still (300px), all left-aligned 64px into the stage.
sections.mobile: Names become one sideways-scrolling row at 22px with scroll-snap, the selected one in full ink. Beneath, the stage fills the width and is 70svh tall; the sheet keeps its true size, anchored top-left with a 16px inset and cropped by the stage's right and bottom edges. Tapping a name swaps it.

sections.name: Small proof beside text
sections.blueprint: One narrow module repeated four to six times down the page, never alternating sides. Each module is 640px wide at most and starts on the page's text margin (at about 22% of the viewport on an understated page). Left part: a flat panel 360px wide and 120 to 200px tall, one tone off the ground, radius 8px, holding one small exact demonstration: a cropped interface fragment at true size, or a tightly cropped photograph covering the panel. Right part, 20px away and top-aligned: a heading of one or two lines at 18px medium and two short paragraphs at 15px in the soft ink, in a column 250px wide. Panel heights vary with their content; text always hangs from the panel's top edge. 96–120px of empty ground between modules. The section heading is 24–28px, on the same left edge, 64px above the first module. In a column under 600px the text moves beneath its panel.
sections.mobile: Each module stacks: the panel at full width and natural height, then heading and paragraphs 16px below on the same left edge, at 17px and 15px. 64px between modules. Panels keep their true-size contents and crop from the right instead of scaling down.

sections.name: Day tabs, banded agenda
sections.blueprint: A two-line heading at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), first line in the soft ink and second in full ink, with the booking button on the same row at the far right. 56px below, left: a 150px column of stacked day tabs, each a filled block 150 by 64px with 6px gaps showing the weekday at 16px and the date at 13px; the active tab takes the darkest fill with inverted text. Right, from 190px to the right margin: the day's sessions as alternating tone bands, each 76px tall with an 8px radius and 4px gaps, the two tones one step apart. Inside a band, on fixed column starts: the time at 20px with tabular figures, 20px from the left; the title at 18px in medium weight at 22%, with a one-line note at 13px in the soft ink under it; speaker names right-aligned at 14px beside up to three overlapping 32px round portraits.
sections.mobile: The heading stacks above a full-width button. Day tabs become a horizontal row of equal filled blocks, sticky under the top edge. Each band stacks time over title over speakers with 16px padding and grows to fit; portraits sit at the band's top-right corner.

sections.name: Drag through the stages
sections.blueprint: A 50/50 split, 88svh tall: two flat fields meeting on a clean vertical edge, and one slider that drives both. Left field: the current stage as a clause of three to six words at clamp(40px, 4.6vw, 76px) on two lines, top-left from column 1, starting with its order word; it serves as the heading. Right field: one fragment of the product at true size, about 440px wide, centred, root marked data-ui, in the state that matches the clause. Along the bottom, crossing both fields inside 28px margins, a real range `<input>` with four stops: a solid track 8px tall, the part already passed in full ink, and a square thumb 32px across in the accent. Under the track, four stage names at 16px, the current one in full ink. Dragging, or the arrow keys, swaps the clause and the fragment's state with a 200ms crossfade; nothing depends on scroll.
sections.mobile: The fragment's field comes first, 46svh, the fragment at true size and cropped to its active region. The slider follows directly beneath on the seam, thumb 40px. Then the clause field: the clause at 9vw on two lines, with the four stage names under it in a two-by-two block at 15px.

sections.name: Accordion of filled tiles
sections.blueprint: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, `position: sticky; top: 96px` so it stays while the list scrolls past. Columns 5–12 hold the accordion: each question is a filled tile one step from the page ground, with 8px between tiles, no border and the page's one radius (or its motif's corner). A closed tile is 72px tall with the question at 20px medium on the left, 24px padding, and on the right a plus sign drawn from two 3px bars 16px long. The open tile switches to the accent colour with its assigned ink, the plus becomes a minus by rotating one bar, and the answer appears at 17px, no wider than 52ch. Build each tile as `<details>` with a shared `name` so one opens at a time. Six to nine tiles.
sections.mobile: The heading sits above at 9vw, not sticky. Tiles run full width with 6px gaps, questions at 18px wrapping to two lines, closed height at least 64px. The open tile keeps the accent colour, and answers are set at 16px with 20px padding.

sections.name: A sentence with a blank
sections.blueprint: The closing sentence has a gap in it, and the gap is the form. A sentence of five to eight words is set at about 6vw on two lines, flush left across columns 1–11; there is no separate heading. Where the reader's email (or name, or city) belongs, an `<input>` sits inline on the baseline: a filled block of the one-step tone, exactly one line-height tall and about 7em wide, with the placeholder in the same face and size in the softer ink, no border, and the page's radius or motif corner. The sentence's last word is the submit `<button>`, set in the same type on a block of the accent colour of the same height. Field and button use `em` units so they scale with the sentence. One line at 16px under the sentence, in the softer ink, says what happens after sending. Nothing else is in the section.
sections.mobile: The sentence is set at 10vw on two lines; the input drops to a line of its own between them at full width and one line-height tall, and the final word, as the button, ends the second line. The explaining line follows at 15px.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Typewave
references.idea: A plugin about type scales sold on a near-black page where flat saturated fields (orange, lime, blue) act as stages for the plugin's own dark interface.
references.hero: Near-black field. Nav row at the top: pixel-block logo and wordmark left, four plain links centred (one carrying a tiny lime tag), a cream rectangular button with a Figma glyph right. The headline sits centred around mid-height: three lines at about 6.7vw, medium weight, off-white, with the third line recoloured pale lime. Below it a three-line 18px paragraph held to about 45% of the width, then a small cream button repeating the nav action. About 150px lower, the top edge of a flat orange slab, 70% of the viewport wide with barely rounded corners, peeks over the fold; it holds the plugin window.
references.type: Roobert throughout: weight 500 for the 96px headline with slight negative tracking, 16-18px body, 28px card headings, about four sizes in all. Sentence case everywhere; the only emphasis device is recolouring one headline line.
references.colour: #0f0f0e #191918 #e6e3da #f88616 #e4f283 #1463ff — Warm near-black ground with cream text. Orange, lime and electric blue never colour paragraphs; they only fill the rectangles behind product screenshots and the matching step-number chips.
references.imagery: Dark plugin windows with a soft drop shadow, floated centred on flat saturated rectangles (orange, lime, blue, one pink); the rectangles are near square-cornered and inset inside a slightly lighter dark card.
references.layout: Centred hero, then a 1000px container of full-width dark cards, each split one-third text and two-thirds colour stage. Export features alternate text and tile left to right. A small two-button bar stays pinned bottom-centre.

sections.description: Three stacked cards in a slightly lighter black, each about 1000 by 350px. Left third: a 16px square number chip in the card's accent colour at the top, a three-line 28px heading under it, and a grey 12px paragraph pushed to the card's bottom edge, leaving a tall gap between. Right two-thirds: a flat colour rectangle inset 16px with the dark plugin window centred and shadowed on it. Cards differ only by hue: lime, orange, blue.

Between demo blocks a single left-aligned sentence at about 36px sits alone on black with some 300px of space above and below. Its words light up from dark grey to cream one after another as you scroll, so mid-capture the sentence trails off into the background. The pinned two-button bar is the only other element on screen.

Export options as alternating rows. One side: a square colour tile (lime, then orange) holding a code-panel screenshot. Other side: a 24px heading, a five-line grey paragraph and a row of three or four small monochrome tool logos. Tile and text swap sides on each row, and the tiles are staggered vertically so one row's tile overlaps the next row's text band.

steal: Stage dark UI screenshots on flat saturated rectangles instead of on the page background, so the colour does the branding and the UI stays legible.
Pin the paragraph to the bottom of a tall card and the heading to the top so the gap between them becomes the card's composition.
Colour-key each step: the number chip and the stage behind the screenshot share one hue and nothing else on the card uses it.

references.name: Shelf
references.idea: Saves scattered across a dozen places are funnelled into one searchable shelf, shown literally by tumbling source chips and a panel edge that narrows to a point.
references.hero: An off-white panel sits inside a 12px warm-grey page frame. A compact floating nav about 880px wide: logo left, three links and a lime waitlist button right. Centred stack: a small grey pill badge with a sparkle icon, then a two-line headline in General Sans Semibold at about 5.8vw with tight tracking, one word of which sits on a lime rounded-rectangle highlight; a two-line grey subhead; an email field with its button nested inside one rounded outline, 460px wide. From 75% down, the top of a bordered app window rises, and a larger search bar holding a half-typed query overlaps it with a soft shadow.
references.type: General Sans Semibold for headings (84px hero, 40 to 50px section heads, -0.03em); Switzer for everything else at 14 to 20px, mostly mid-grey. About four sizes. The one flourish is a headline word set on a coloured block.
references.colour: #fbfbf9 #f2f1ed #1b1b19 #9ee86f #e9e9e6 — Warm off-whites and soft charcoal with one lime green: the nav button, the highlighted word, small tags and a full-colour closing block.
references.imagery: Vector mock-ups of the app: a bordered window with sidebar and save cards, an enlarged search field, tiny wireframe thumbnails in step cards. No photography. Angled pill chips with small source icons act as illustration.
references.layout: Centred column inside large rounded off-white panels separated by the grey page frame. Mostly stacked heading-plus-subtext blocks, one left and right split, one narrow accordion column. Panel edges are shaped: one ends in a shallow downward chevron.

sections.description: A centred heading and two-line subtext are partly covered by about nine grey pill chips, each naming a save source with a small icon, rotated at random angles as if dropped. The panel's bottom edge is a shallow V pointing down at centre; from its tip a thin vertical line descends about 80px to a second centred heading, subtext and an empty search field, so the layout itself draws a funnel.

A rounded white panel split in two. Left, from a 10% inset: a small lime tag with icon, a two-line heading at about 50px and two short grey paragraphs, vertically centred. Right, from 53% to 90%: three stacked rounded grey cards about 130px tall, each with a white thumbnail tile at left (a tiny wireframe or the logo) and at right a black numbered dot, a bold one-line title and a line or two of grey text.

A lime rounded block about two-thirds of the width, flanked by narrower lime blocks at left and right separated by 14px gaps, as if cropped from a row. Inside, left-aligned and vertically centred: a 40px heading, two lines of small text and a white email field with the button nested in it. A one-line footer sits on a white strip below.

steal: Shape a section's bottom edge into a chevron and run a hairline from its tip to the next heading, turning 'many into one' into layout.
Overlap an enlarged, half-typed search field onto the product window so the hero shows the key interaction rather than a whole screenshot.
Frame the page as rounded panels inside a slightly darker margin so sections read as stacked sheets.

references.name: Vectr
references.idea: An industrial staffing service tells its process as a flight over a miniature clay world: one fixed WebGL diorama of plants, warehouses, wind turbines and tiny workers in a single matte pale blue that matches the page ground, crossed by a glowing blue trail that runs from a headquarters building past a campus and a grid of work positions and ends at the brand mark itself.
references.hero: On a pale steel-blue ground, a fixed full-viewport canvas in the same colour, its fog fading into the page so the scene has no edge: an isometric matte miniature industrial town (tower blocks, a warehouse, wind turbines, crates, tiny figures) fills the lower ~60%, cropped by the bottom and right edges. In the open fog above, a two-line 96px (6.7vw) headline, weight 500, -0.06em, leading 0.9, is centred and about 700px wide from y≈115, with a three-line 18px subline at y≈350 doing the real explaining. A transparent 80px nav: two small links at the left, the wordmark centred, a frosted apply pill and a near-black request pill at the right; an underlined scroll prompt at the bottom centre.
references.type: Roboto alone at 400 and 500: a 96px hero (6.7vw, -0.06em, leading 0.9), an 80px closing line, 64px section headlines (-0.04em), 36px footer cells, 24px step and FAQ titles, 18px body (the bulk of the characters), and 12-14px uppercase nav and button labels. All the typographic character comes from a custom extended geometric wordmark, used at about 90px in the nav and 1344px wide in the footer.
references.colour: #d0e1eb #fcfcfc #050419 #585765 #3932dc — Pale steel blue for the first 43% of the page (canvas and fog), then white, then near-black indigo for the closing call and the footer. Text is mostly a muted slate (about 4.6:1 on the blue, less over the model; the house rules want running text in the full ink). One electric indigo for the logo, the footer arrows and the light trail; a red beam is the only warm signal.
references.imagery: A monochrome clay render: every object matte pale blue-white with soft ambient-occlusion shadows and low contrast, colour kept for signals (a cyan-to-indigo light trail, a dot glow under the active area, a red incoming beam, the indigo mark). Black isometric pictograms at the camera's angle for the features, and one warm photograph of three hard-hatted workers on a gantry, with about 12px corners, that breaks the world.
references.layout: 18px nav insets; content at 40 or 48px margins. The fixed canvas sits behind the first ~4700px, with a 900px sticky stage over 3.8 screens for four steps and a pinned feature row over 3.3 screens, then normal flow: a photo split (656x400 picture at x=40, text from x=830), a two-half FAQ, a dark closing block and a three-cell footer row at a 480px pitch. 12.1 screens for 326 words.

sections.description: A 900px sticky stage where the camera stops at four vignettes: the headquarters building wearing the logo, taking in a red beam and sending out the blue trail; a hangar campus the trail sweeps through; a field of white square tiles with one raised and a figure on it; and finally the brand mark as a glowing indigo object in a halo of cyan dots. The step list is docked bottom-left at x=48 in a column about 600px wide: inactive steps as 14px rows, the active one with a 24px title and an 18px body.

A white panel slides up over the canvas with a two-line 64px headline at x=40, and a row of four 350px cards fills in one per scroll step, each with a black isometric pictogram, a 20px title and a short 14px body.

Split: a warm photograph of three workers in hi-vis on a plant gantry, 656x400 (46% of the width), at the left margin, and from x=830 a three-line 64px headline, a two-line paragraph and a dark 48px pill, the group centred on the picture.

A near-black indigo block: an 80px two-line closing line at x=40 with a white pill under it, a full-width row of three 480x200 cells each with a 36px page name and an electric-blue arrow, then the extended wordmark in white across 93% of the width and a 12px legal row.

steal: Set a WebGL scene's clear colour and fog to the exact page ground, render the whole world in one matte clay tone, and keep colour for two or three signals: one bright trail, one contrasting incoming beam, the brand colour on the mark.

Tell an N-step process as N camera stops in one persistent scene, about 0.95 screens of scroll per step, the step list docked bottom-left and the focal object centre-right, and end the last stop on the brand mark so the journey has a destination. The site numbers its steps; the house version shows order by position and by the active step's size.

Let one neutral grotesk do all the reading and give the personality to a custom extended wordmark, repeated across 93% of the width to close the footer. The site's four icon-topped feature cards drop back into a generic kit; the house version keeps the world going with a section blueprint instead.
references.media: One fixed WebGL canvas covers 100% of the first screen, the clay town in the lower ~60% and fog in the ground colour above it, and stays behind the first ~4700px as camera stops for the steps; then one 656x400 photograph in a split, four 96px pictograms and a giant SVG wordmark. No video.
references.motion: A 2.5-4s CSS loader turns the mark from -60 degrees to 0 over 1.5s and draws two orbits over about 2s, then hero lines rise and fade over 1.5s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) at 0.1-0.5s staggers after the canvas fades in over 0.7s. Lenis moves the camera between four stops, swapping step copy over 0.5s on the same expo-out curve (44 uses in all) and opening the active body by grid-template-rows over 0.6s, while the pinned feature row adds one card per step; there is no reduced-motion rule.
